capitals.note: Infobox 'Kota Batu (1368-1660)'; the text puts the move to Kota Batu in 1397.

capitals.name: Brunei Town, Kampong Ayer (now Bandar Seri Begawan)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Brunei Town, Kampong Ayer (1660-1920)'; Brunei Town is today's Bandar Seri Begawan.

keyframe_review.note: 4,799 km2: Brunei Bay with Kota Batu on the Brunei River (Brunei and Muara, parts of Tutong and Belait, five Sarawak cells). The page dates the first ruler 'Reign 1363/68-1402' and Kota Batu '1368-1660'. Infobox gives no area. The same page has the Nagarakretagama naming Barune as Majapahit's vassal in 1365; the Majapahit dossier carries that tint.

49,192 km2: the coast of north-west Borneo (Sarawak, the Sabah west coast, Labuan, five Kalimantan Barat cells). Matches the page: under Bolkiah (1485-1524) 'the sultanate controlled the coastal areas of northwest Borneo'; the page dates no step inside the reign, so 1492 is Cliopatria's year. Infobox gives no area.

correction.text: the north-west Borneo coast only; Manila removed ('not considered to have extended to military or political rule')

keyframe_review.note: 50,132 km2: adds five cells at Manila (Manila, Makati, Pasay, Mandaluyong, San Juan). The Maynila page says Brunei's influence at Manila 'is not considered to have extended to military or political rule' and describes only intermarriage and trade (Manila 'probably founded as a Bornean trading colony about 1500'); the Bruneian Empire page says Brunei 'gained influence in Luzon'. Influence, not territory: the Manila cells are removed. The Borneo part is unchanged.

correction.text: the north-west Borneo coast only; Manila removed

keyframe_review.note: 104,357 km2: the coast of north-west Borneo doubles (Sabah 165 cells, Sarawak 141, Brunei complete) with Manila still attached. Borneo part kept as 'the coastal areas of northwest Borneo' (Bruneian Empire page); Manila removed as for 1497. The step has no page date (Cliopatria's year).

correction.text: north-west Borneo and Palawan as drawn; the Sulu Archipelago becomes a vassal tint; Manila removed

keyframe_review.note: 124,386 km2: adds Palawan and the Sulu Archipelago (Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, Basilan). The Bolkiah page: Bolkiah 'defeated the states of Suluk and Seludang' and his dominion is said to have included 'Manila and the Sulu Archipelago'; the Bruneian Empire page has 'Brunei's influence extended to the southern Philippines'. Neither is dated, and Sulu keeps its own dynasty and court, so the archipelago is drawn as a tributary tint (vassal events 1507-1578), Manila is removed, and Palawan stays as Cliopatria draws it: no page opened mentions Palawan (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: north-west Borneo and Palawan; no Mindanao, no Manila; the Sulu Archipelago as vassal tint

keyframe_review.note: 230,860 km2, the largest shape: adds the whole of Mindanao (Zamboanga to Davao, Butuan, Cotabato, Lanao, Bukidnon, 332 cells). No page opened puts Mindanao under Brunei: the Bruneian Empire page speaks of influence 'to the southern Philippines (Taguima/Basilan)' at most, and Cliopatria's own Sultanate of Maguindanao row begins in 1521 on the same cells and takes over 332 of them in 1582. Mindanao and Manila are removed; the Sulu Archipelago is tint; Palawan as drawn. Infobox gives no area; the corrected shape is about 379 cells, 52% of the drawn one.

117,121 km2: north-west Borneo and Palawan after the Castilian War. 'In the resulting Castilian War, the Spanish took Sulu and in April captured Brunei itself', driven out after 72 days; 'Sulu regained its independence soon after'. Cliopatria's 332 Mindanao cells pass to Maguindanao, nine to Sulu (kept out of this dossier's corrected shapes). Palawan is unverified.
120,204 km2: the 1582 shape plus five cells in Palawan and Sabah; nothing on the pages dates it. Kept (unverified: page budget).

119,110 km2: three cells go to Cliopatria's Sultanate of Sambas, which begins in 1619; the Bruneian Empire page says Sambas 'developed dynastic relations with Brunei's royal house'. Kept (unverified: page budget); the ledger records the three cells as a Sambas loss at confidence 1.
112,142 km2: 21 cells of north Palawan pass to Cliopatria's Spanish Empire. No page opened dates Spain's Palawan footholds; kept (unverified: page budget), ledger loss at confidence 1.

68,701 km2: 147 cells of Sabah (the north and east) pass to the Sultanate of Sulu at the end of the civil war of 1661-1673: 'The Sultan of Sulu ... claimed that he was asked by Brunei to help and was promised eastern Sabah as a reward' (disputed). The Sabah west coast, 19 cells, stays with Brunei, matching the North Borneo page, where Brunei grants the Putatan River and the Padas district only in 1884 and concessions in 1877-1878. Kept.

correction.text: as drawn without Labuan (British from 1846); Saribas and Skrang go in 1852 (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: 54,678 km2: Sarawak proper (Kuching) is gone: 'Hashim granted Sarawak to Brooke on 24 September 1841', confirmed by July 1842; 26 Palawan cells pass to Spain in the same year (page silent). Labuan is still inside the shape although 'Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddin II ceded Labuan to the British under the Treaty of Labuan' in 1846 (History of Brunei); Labuan is removed from 1846 on. The shape holds Saribas and Skrang until 1852 (Raj of Sarawak page) where Cliopatria drops them in 1859.

correction.text: as drawn without Labuan; the Rajang River basin goes in 1861 (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: 52,257 km2: Skrang is gone ('In 1852, the new Sultan ceded the Saribas and Skrang districts ... to Brooke'; Cliopatria's year is 1859). Labuan removed (British from 1846). The Rajang basin goes in 1861 on the page; Cliopatria keeps it to 1869.
51,558 km2: four cells to Sarawak (no page date). Labuan removed; the Rajang basin goes in 1861 on the page and Cliopatria keeps it to 1869.

correction.text: as drawn without Labuan; the Sabah coast is leased from 1877 and ceded in 1884 (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: 21,689 km2: 93 cells to Sarawak (Rajang basin, Bintulu, Mukah, Baram). 'In 1861, he acquired the Rajang River basin, which subsequently became the Third Division' (Raj of Sarawak page); Bintulu, Mukah and Baram are not dated on any page opened (Baram is the 1882 acquisition of other sources, not read). Labuan removed. The Sabah west coast is kept to 1884: the North Borneo page has 'land concessions in northern Borneo from the Sultanate of Brunei and Sulu' in 1877-1878, the Putatan River in May 1884 and the Padas district in November 1884; the ledger draws the 1877-1884 coast as a lease.

11,843 km2: the Sabah coast has passed to the British North Borneo company (Putatan and Padas 1884) and Trusan goes to Sarawak in 1885 ('Brunei later agreed to cede Trusan in 1885'). Limbang is still inside; it is annexed on 17 March 1890. Cliopatria ends the row in 1889.

correction.text: the Sultanate of Brunei as a British protectorate: Brunei-Muara, Tutong, Belait and Temburong, divided by Sarawak's Limbang

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 1890-1986, but the Sultanate went on as a British protectorate: 'signed the Protectorate Agreement on 17 September 1888', a Resident from 1905-1906, independence on 1 January 1984. The shape is Cliopatria's 1987 outline (7,272 km2), Brunei in two parts after Limbang went to Sarawak in 1890. Infobox gives no area.
7,272 km2 for independent Brunei (from 1 January 1984); the pages give no area to compare.

region.text: Brunei Bay with Kota Batu on the Brunei River

ledger.note: 1363: the Sultanate of Brunei at Kota Batu. The page's infobox gives the first ruler's 'Reign 1363/68-1402' and the capital 'Kota Batu (1368-1660)'; the article is titled Bruneian Sultanate (1368-1888). The page names the capital and Brunei Bay, not a boundary.

region.text: the coastal areas of northwest Borneo: Sarawak, the Sabah west coast, Labuan

ledger.note: c. 1492: the coast of north-west Borneo is Brunei's. 'the sultanate controlled the coastal areas of northwest Borneo' under Bolkiah (reign 1485-1524); the page dates no step inside the reign, so 1492 is Cliopatria's year. No state is named on the coast.

c. 1502: the Borneo coast widens inland and along Sabah (Cliopatria: Sabah 165 cells, Sarawak 141). The Bolkiah page gives Bolkiah 'essentially all of coastal Borneo' and rule 'as far south as Banjarmasin' without years; only the north-west part is kept (see the 1512 keyframe).

c. 1507: Sulu under Brunei's sphere. 'Defeated the states of Suluk and Seludang' (Silsilah, as the Bolkiah page quotes it) and 'Manila and the Sulu Archipelago' in his dominion, undated; Bolkiah also married the daughter of the Sulu sultan. The year is Cliopatria's (its Sulu row has a gap 1507-1528). A tint, not territory: Sulu keeps its sultan.
1578: Sulu is free. 'Sulu regained its independence soon after' the Castilian War; the page gives no year beyond the war. Cliopatria returns its Sulu row in 1529, not 1578.
April 1578: the Spanish take Brunei Town. 'In the resulting Castilian War, the Spanish took Sulu and in April captured Brunei itself.'
26 June 1578: the Spanish leave. The Sultan's forces drove them out 'after only 72 days of Domination and Spanish returned to Manila on 26 June 1578'.

region.text: the three cells that become Sambas

ledger.note: 1619: three cells to Sambas. The page says only that Sambas 'developed dynastic relations with Brunei's royal house'; Cliopatria's Sultanate of Sambas row begins in 1619.
c. 1629: north Palawan passes to Spain (Cliopatria: 21 cells go to its Spanish Empire shape). No page opened dates Spain's Palawan posts or Brunei's hold on Palawan.

c. 1660: the capital moves from Kota Batu to Brunei Town on the water village of Kampong Ayer (infobox: 'Kota Batu (1368-1660)', 'Brunei Town, Kampong Ayer (1660-1920)'); the page links the end of the old capital to the civil war.

region.text: eastern Sabah, the area Sulu says it was promised

ledger.note: 1673: eastern Sabah to Sulu, at the end of the civil war (1661-1673). 'The Sultan of Sulu, however, claimed that he was asked by Brunei to help and was promised eastern Sabah as a reward'; 'It is not clear to historians whether Muhyiddin asked for Sulu's help'; the body names Kimanis. Cliopatria hands 147 Sabah cells to the Sultanate of Sulu in 1673; the date of an actual transfer is the shape's, not the page's.

region.text: Sarawak proper: 'Hashim granted Sarawak to Brooke'

ledger.note: 24 September 1841: Brunei grants Sarawak to James Brooke. 'Hashim granted Sarawak to Brooke on 24 September 1841'; 'by July 1842, his appointment was confirmed by Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddin II'. The grant was Sarawak proper (the Kuching region); Cliopatria's Kingdom of Sarawak row begins 1842.
c. 1842: Palawan passes to Spain (Cliopatria: 26 cells go to its Spanish Empire shape in 1842). Page silent on Palawan.

1846: Labuan to Britain. 'Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddin II ceded Labuan to the British under the Treaty of Labuan' in 1846; the Treaty of Friendship and Commerce of 1847 'officially ceded' it. Cliopatria keeps Labuan inside Brunei's shape to 1884.
1852: Saribas and Skrang to Brooke. 'In 1852, the new Sultan ceded the Saribas and Skrang districts, which later became the Second Division, to Brooke.' Cliopatria drops the cells in 1859.

1861: the Rajang River basin to Brooke. 'In 1861, he acquired the Rajang River basin, which subsequently became the Third Division.' Cliopatria drops 93 cells in 1870 (Rajang basin, Bintulu, Mukah, Baram); the page does not mention Bintulu, Oya, Mukah or Baram.
c. 1868: four more Sarawak cells (Cliopatria's year; no page opened dates it).

region.text: the Sarawak coast between the Rajang and the Baram

ledger.note: c. 1870: the rest of the Sarawak coast between the Rajang and the Baram to Brooke (Cliopatria: 93 cells to its Kingdom of Sarawak shape in 1870). The Rajang basin part is the page's 1861; Bintulu, Mukah, Baram are undated on the pages opened (a gap-filler should open the Baram and Bintulu articles).

region.text: stretches to the east of the capital, leased in 1877

ledger.note: 1877: the Sabah coast leased to the North Borneo company. The North Borneo page: 'founded in 1877-1878 through a series of land concessions in northern Borneo from the Sultanate of Brunei and Sulu'; the History of Brunei page: 'in 1877, stretches to the east of the capital were leased (later ceded) to the British'. Hatched until the cessions of 1884; the boundary of the lease is not on either page.
May 1884: the Putatan River ceded. The North Borneo page lists 'the Putatan River (May 1884)' among Brunei's cessions to the Chartered Company.

November 1884: the Padas district ceded. The North Borneo page: 'the Padas district (November 1884)'; the Limbang page has 'Padas in 1887' (a different cession or a different date, unresolved). Cliopatria drops the Sabah coast in 1885.
November 1884: the lease of 1877 ends in cession, the Sabah coast being the company's.

1885: Trusan to Sarawak. 'Brunei later agreed to cede Trusan in 1885 and Padas in 1887.' The page gives no boundary; the circle is the researcher's placement of the Trusan district (the gazetteer lacks Trusan and Lawas). [Reviewer se-02-c: region was a 35 km circle round 4.8 N 115.35 E, which reaches Bangar in Temburong (about 33 km); now the Sarawak part of what the 1870 shape loses by 1885.]

17 September 1888: Brunei becomes a British protectorate. 'On 17 September 1888, Brunei signed an agreement with Great Britain which formally put Brunei under British protectorate' (the History of Brunei page: 'signed the Protectorate Agreement on 17 September 1888'); a Resident from the 1905-1906 Supplementary Treaty. The Sultanate continues under the same dynasty, so it is a status change (the British dossier carries the protectorate tint), not a new state.

17 March 1890: Limbang annexed. 'On 17 March 1890, Rajah Charles Brooke annexed Limbang, subjected to the approval of the British government'; in August 1892 the governor of the Straits Settlements 'decided that Sarawak should possess Limbang' and in August 1895 the Colonial Office 'considered the case closed despite no agreement being reached'. Brunei is cut in two. [Reviewer se-02-c: region was a 40 km circle round 4.75 N 115.0 E, which holds Bandar Seri Begawan (about 17 km away) and Temburong; now the Sarawak part of the 1885 shape that the 1987 shape lacks, i.e. Limbang between the two halves of Brunei (Limbang page).]
December 1941: the Japanese occupy Brunei. The Sultan received 'decorations and a salary upon the country's surrender to the Japanese Army during World War II in December 1941'.
June 1945: Brunei is liberated. 'when Australian forces liberated Brunei in June 1945'; military rule until July 1946.

1 January 1984: independence. 'Brunei gained its independence from the United Kingdom on 1 January 1984'; the 1959 Constitution of 29 September 1959 had ended British control. The state is Brunei Darussalam from then.

wars.name: Castilian War
wars.outcome: The Spanish took Sulu and in April 1578 captured Brunei Town; driven out after 72 days (back in Manila on 26 June 1578). Sulu regained its independence soon after.

wars.name: Bruneian Civil War of 1660

zones.text: eastern Sabah, the area Sulu claims it was promised

wars.outcome: Muhyiddin defeated and killed Abdul Hakkul Mubin; Sulu says it helped and was promised eastern Sabah, a claim that persists.
wars.note: The article is titled 1660 but its body and infobox use 1661-1673.

wars.name: Brooke's conflict with the Sultan
wars.outcome: 'In 1843, an open conflict between Brooke and the Sultan ended in the latter's defeat.' No territory is dated to it.

wars.name: Limbang annexation
wars.outcome: Charles Brooke annexed Limbang on 17 March 1890; the British decided in August 1892 that Sarawak should keep it; the case was 'considered closed' in August 1895 without agreement.

certainty.note: A coastal and riverine sultanate: no surveyed boundary; the Sarawak and Sabah frontiers are cessions of districts and river basins without lines.
The cessions of 1884-1885, the decision on Limbang in 1892 and the protectorate fix the Sarawak and Sabah frontiers on paper; Limbang was never agreed by the Sultan (1895).

notes:
ONE STATE, NOT TWO. The brief suspects successive states in Cliopatria's 1363-2024 row. The pages opened show one sultanate under one dynasty: the Bruneian Empire to 1888, a British protectorate from 17 September 1888 ('The protectorate lasted until 1984'), independent Brunei Darussalam from 1 January 1984. It is kept as one dossier, with 1888 and 1984 as rename events; the colour agent may wish to tint 1888-1983 as a protectorate (the British dossier would carry the matching vassal_start, not this one). Cliopatria has no shape 1890-1986; keyframe sultanate-of-brunei_1890 supplies it from the 1987 outline.

SHAPES THE PAGES CONTRADICT. (1) The 1497-1511 Manila cells and the 1512 Mindanao cells (332) have no support: the Maynila page says Brunei's influence 'is not considered to have extended to military or political rule'. (2) The Sulu Archipelago is drawn as a tributary tint 1507-1578 on the Bolkiah and History of Brunei pages (undated, hence confidence 1 at the start); the Sulu dossier may disagree. (3) Palawan (Cliopatria 1507-1841) is not mentioned on any page opened; kept as drawn, flagged. (4) The Sabah west coast stays Brunei's to 1884 in Cliopatria, consistent with the North Borneo page; the 1877 concession is drawn as a lease.

PAGE DATES vs CLIOPATRIA YEARS (Sarawak): grant of Sarawak proper 1841 (Cliopatria 1842), Saribas and Skrang 1852 (1859), Rajang basin 1861 (1870, which also holds Bintulu, Mukah and Baram, undated on the pages opened). The Charles Brooke article was opened for Baram, Trusan and Limbang and holds none; Limbang page supplied Trusan 1885 and Limbang 1890. Baram (1882 in other sources) is not recorded. Padas is 'November 1884' (North Borneo) and '1887' (Limbang): unresolved.

PAGE BUDGET (9): Bruneian Empire, History of Brunei, Bolkiah, Raj of Sarawak, Charles Brooke (empty for this purpose), Limbang, North Borneo, Bruneian Civil War of 1660 (after the Brunei_Civil_War disambiguation page), Maynila: ten pages opened and listed (the Bolkiah_of_Brunei URL also failed to load); over the budget of nine because three yielded nothing for this purpose (Charles Brooke, the disambiguation page, the failed URL). Not opened: Castilian War, Sultanate of Sulu, Brunei Revolt, British protectorate of Brunei, Labuan, the sultans' list (no ruler strip written).

COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT A DOSSIER: british-colonial-empire stands for the Colony of Labuan and the British North Borneo company (Chartered Company), which have no row in polities.csv (Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire touches Brunei in 1880-1889 and 1987-1995); a North Borneo dossier (1877/1881-1946) is for the se-03 group. Gazetteer lacks Limbang, Lawas, Trusan, Kota Batu, Kudat, Sambas; stand-ins are coordinates with radius.

AREA: the Bruneian Empire infobox gives no area, so no keyframe could be compared; the 1512 shape as drawn is 230,860 km2 against about 119,000 km2 corrected (cell count 379 of 731).
